text: Step back and look at the whole membrane. Every carbohydrate chain in it, on the glycolipid and on both glycoproteins, is on the top face, outside the cell; none faces the cytoplasm. Cholesterol is in both layers, but the glycolipid is in the outer layer. As a description you could write: cholesterol sits between the phospholipids in both layers, its O H group towards the heads; glycolipids and glycoproteins have carbohydrate chains that project from the outer surface of the membrane.
